title: Dataset of an EEG-based BCI experiment in Virtual Reality using P300
description: EEG recordings from 21 healthy participants performing a visual P300 brain-computer interface task (6x6 speller matrix of flashing crosses) in two conditions: on a personal computer and in virtual reality with a passive smartphone-based head-mounted display. The dataset was collected to compare P300-based BCI performance and user experience across the two platforms. Signals were recorded from 16 electrodes at 512 Hz at GIPSA-lab in 2018.
methods_description: Each participant completed two randomized sessions (PC and VR), each with 12 blocks of 5 repetitions. Each repetition consisted of 12 flashes of groups of 6 symbols, so every symbol flashed exactly twice. EEG was recorded with a g.USBamp amplifier and 16 wet electrodes in an EasyCap (10-10 montage), referenced to the right earlobe with ground at AFZ. Stimulation was delivered by the Unity engine, and VR used a VRElegiant HMD with a Huawei Mate 7 smartphone. Events were tagged via USB with a mean latency of about 38 ms on PC and 117 ms in VR.
